nodes.one_liner: The core shift: model decides actions, not just text

nodes.title: The agent loop

outline.rationale: The user already ships an LLM app, so I skip prompt/API basics entirely and skip research theory and framework comparisons (explicitly deprioritized). The first five nodes build the conceptual mental model the user lacks: the agent-vs-LLM distinction, tool use, the loop, planning, and the crucial "is it worth it" judgment — each addressing a distinct facet with low overlap. Reliability is included because anyone shipping an agent needs to handle loops/cost/failures, which is build-relevant rather than theoretical. The final node delivers on their stated goal of integrating one into their existing app, deliberately framed around extending what they already have. Order is roughly dependency-based: distinction → mechanics (tools, loop) → higher-level behavior (planning) → judgment → robustness → integration.
